title: Exact fermionic dual of the Bose-Hubbard model
authors: Lei Su, Ivar Martin, Aashish A. Clerk
abstract: Recent developments have established exact bosonization and fermionization with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry as dualities through gauging. In this work, we apply fermionic gauging, which realizes generalized Jordan-Wigner transformations, to the Bose-Hubbard (BH) model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry and derive an exact dual description in terms of fermionic composites, built from bosons and fermions. In 1D, this duality generalizes the exact mapping between the extended hard-core BH model and the spinless Fermi-Hubbard model to now cover soft-core interactions. At low energies, the mapping reduces to the well-known equivalence between the sine-Gordon model and the Thirring model. The oscillation wave vector of the fermionic composite correlation function in the gapless phase is fixed by their density, providing a novel manifestation of Luttinger's theorem. We verify the exact duality using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations and demonstrate that the gapless phase and the phase transition are governed by the compact boson conformal field theory. Our construction naturally extends to generic bosonic systems and higher dimensions, opening new avenues for studying Bose-Fermi mixtures in optical lattices and other strongly correlated quantum systems.
summary: This work establishes an exact fermionic dual for the Bose-Hubbard model by employing fermionic gauging techniques. It shows that the model can be recast into a fermionic description, whose low-energy behavior is captured by the sine-Gordon model. This provides a powerful, unified theoretical framework for studying strongly correlated bosonic and fermionic quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper derives an exact fermionic dual description for the Bose-Hubbard (BH) model, extending known duality mappings.
main_result: An exact dual Hamiltonian is constructed in terms of boson-fermion composite operators, revealing that the low-energy physics is governed by the sine-Gordon model.
method: The core method involves applying fermionic gauging to the BH model's U(1) symmetry, realizing generalized Jordan-Wigner transformations, and analyzing the resulting low-energy effective field theory.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Bose-Hubbard (BH) model, which describes interacting bosons on a lattice. The analysis extends this to include fermionic composites and is analyzed in 1D and 2D settings.
key_observables: The oscillation wave vector of the fermionic composite correlation function, and the nature of the phase transition (superfluid vs. Mott insulating).
important_parameters: The ratio of interaction strength to hopping ($U/t$), and the filling factor (density).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on unitary disentangling transformations and assumes the applicability of low-energy effective theories like the sine-Gordon model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fermionic gauging process, showing the insertion of Majorana fermions and the resulting structure of the dual Hamiltonian and correlation functions.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by introducing the fermionic gauging procedure to the BH model, deriving the dual Hamiltonian, analyzing the low-energy continuum limit via bosonization (sine-Gordon/Thirring equivalence), and finally discussing boundary effects and generalizations to higher dimensions.
why_interesting: The explicit mapping between bosonic and fermionic descriptions of strongly correlated systems like the BH model provides powerful theoretical tools for understanding quantum phases in optical lattices.

FIG. 5: Fermionic gauging of the 2D Bose-Hubbard model on the square lattice (a) and triangular lattice (b). One b boson is placed on each vertex and a pair of Majo- rana fermions, γ and γ′, is introduced on each edge such that each boson is surrounded by four (six) Majorana fermions. A Gauss law is imposed at each vertex, while a flatness condition is imposed on the eight (six) Majorana fermions surrounding each square (triangular) face.
